name: Data-collection regime
scope: when the procedure learns from interaction data
characteristic: relation between the policy being improved and the policy that produced the data
positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: data-collection regime
negative_test: a procedure consuming a fixed i.i.d. dataset
examples: on-policy, off-policy, offline

name: On-policy
positive_test: updates are computed only from data generated by the current policy
negative_test: reusing data from an earlier policy version
examples: REINFORCE, A2C, PPO, SARSA, MAPPO

name: Off-policy with interaction
positive_test: reuses data from other or older policies while still collecting new data
examples: DQN, SAC, TD3, DDPG, Q-learning

name: Offline
positive_test: never interacts with the environment during learning
negative_test: collecting even a small amount of fresh interaction
examples: BCQ, CQL, IQL, Decision Transformer, behaviour cloning

name: Use of a transition model
characteristic: whether a dynamics model exists and where it came from
positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: use of a transition model
examples: model-free, learned model, given model

name: Model-free
positive_test: never predicts next states or rewards
examples: DQN, PPO, SAC, A3C

name: Learned dynamics model
positive_test: fits a transition or reward model from data and uses it
negative_test: using a simulator or rules supplied exogenously
examples: Dyna, PETS, Dreamer, MuZero, MBPO

name: Given dynamics model
positive_test: uses an exact model of the environment supplied by the problem
examples: value iteration, AlphaZero game rules, MPC with analytic dynamics, iLQR

name: Represented quantity in control
characteristic: which of value or policy is explicitly parameterised
positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: represented quantity in control
examples: value-based, policy-based, actor-critic

name: Value-based
positive_test: acts greedily on a learned value function with no separate policy parameters
examples: Q-learning, DQN, Rainbow, IQN, FQI

name: Policy-based
positive_test: parameterises the policy directly with no learned value baseline
examples: REINFORCE, evolution-strategy policy search, CMA-ES policies

name: Actor-critic
positive_test: parameterises both a policy and a learned value estimate
negative_test: having only one of the two
examples: A2C, PPO, SAC, TD3, IMPALA, MAPPO

name: Temporal abstraction
characteristic: whether the procedure acts over extended sub-behaviours
positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: temporal abstraction
examples: flat, hierarchical

name: Flat control
positive_test: selects one primitive action per environment step
negative_test: selecting a sub-policy that runs for many steps
examples: DQN, PPO, SAC

name: Hierarchical control
positive_test: selects temporally extended options or subgoals with their own termination
negative_test: selecting a primitive action each step
examples: options framework, option-critic, FeUdal, HIRO, HAC

name: Information used to choose a step
scope: to any procedure that searches a parameter or configuration space
characteristic: what information about the objective the step rule consumes
positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: information used to choose a step
negative_test: a procedure with no search at all
examples: first-order, preconditioned, zeroth-order, closed-form, combinatorial, sampling
notes: multi-valued; changed from single-valued after HMC and XGBoost each needed two values

name: First-order gradient
positive_test: uses the gradient, scaled only per coordinate
examples: SGD, momentum, Adam, AdamW, Adafactor, Lion

name: Curvature-preconditioned
positive_test: uses a matrix approximation of curvature across coordinates
examples: L-BFGS, K-FAC, Shampoo, Muon, Gauss-Newton, natural gradient

name: Zeroth-order
positive_test: uses only function evaluations, never derivatives
examples: CMA-ES, OpenAI-ES, Nelder-Mead, random search, simulated annealing

name: Closed-form
positive_test: obtains the solution by solving an equation or decomposition in one shot
negative_test: iterating a step rule to convergence
examples: OLS normal equations, ridge closed form, PCA by SVD, LDA, Platt-free isotonic fit

name: Combinatorial search
positive_test: searches a discrete structure with pruning, DP or enumeration
examples: branch and bound, Viterbi, beam search, Hungarian matching, greedy submodular

name: Sampling-based
positive_test: explores by drawing from a target or proposal distribution, not by descending
examples: Metropolis-Hastings, Gibbs, HMC, NUTS, SMC, Langevin dynamics

name: Data seen per update
characteristic: how much data each parameter update consumes
positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: data seen per update
examples: full-batch, minibatch, per-example, single-pass streaming

name: Full-batch
positive_test: each update uses the entire training set
examples: L-BFGS on full data, batch gradient descent, EM over the full dataset, IRLS

name: Minibatch stochastic
positive_test: each update uses a random subset of fixed size
negative_test: each update uses the full dataset or one example
examples: SGD, Adam, most deep learning

name: Per-example online
positive_test: updates after each individual example, typically without storage
examples: perceptron, online gradient descent, Hogwild! per-sample, online k-means

name: Single-pass streaming
positive_test: each example is seen once and cannot be revisited
examples: streaming k-means, reservoir methods, online change-point detection, sketching

name: Coordination topology
scope: when more than one worker participates
characteristic: who exchanges state with whom during training
positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: coordination topology
examples: single, centralized-sync, centralized-async, decentralized, federated-device, federated-silo

name: Single worker
positive_test: one process holds the whole run
examples: default single-GPU training

name: Centralized synchronous
positive_test: all workers synchronise their updates at a global barrier
examples: all-reduce SGD, FSDP, ZeRO, synchronous pipeline

name: Centralized asynchronous
positive_test: workers push to a shared aggregator without waiting for each other
examples: Hogwild!, Downpour, ASGD, FedBuff

name: Decentralized peer-to-peer
positive_test: workers exchange only with neighbours; there is no aggregator
negative_test: an aggregator or all-reduce over all workers
examples: D-PSGD, gossip SGD, SGP

name: Federated cross-device
positive_test: very many intermittently available clients, each with little data
examples: FedAvg on phones, DP-FedAvg, client sampling

name: Federated cross-silo
positive_test: a small number of persistent organisational parties
examples: hospital or bank consortium FL, split learning across silos

name: Raw-data locality constraint
scope: when data originates in more than one place
characteristic: whether raw data may be moved to one place
positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: raw-data locality constraint
examples: pooled, local-only

name: Pooled
positive_test: raw training data is allowed to be centralised
examples: standard distributed training, data-parallel pretraining

name: Raw data stays local
positive_test: only model updates or statistics cross the party boundary
negative_test: shipping raw examples to a central store
examples: federated learning, split learning, local differential privacy pipelines

name: Formal privacy or security property
scope: when the paper claims a protection property
characteristic: what adversary the guarantee is stated against
positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: formal privacy or security property
examples: differential privacy, secure aggregation, encrypted computation, unlearning

name: Differential privacy
positive_test: a per-example sensitivity bound and a reported epsilon budget
examples: DP-SGD, DP-FedAvg, PATE, DP-FTRL

name: Secure aggregation
positive_test: the aggregator provably cannot see individual updates
negative_test: only the raw data is withheld
examples: secure aggregation protocols, masked summation

name: Encrypted computation
positive_test: computation proceeds on encrypted or secret-shared values
examples: homomorphic-encryption training, secure multiparty computation

name: Removal guarantee
positive_test: provides a stated guarantee that a specific example's influence is gone
examples: SISA, certified removal, exact shard retraining

name: Agent multiplicity
characteristic: how many learning agents interact and with what alignment of interests
positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: agent multiplicity
negative_test: a single predictor on a dataset
examples: single, cooperative, competitive, mixed

name: Single agent
positive_test: one policy interacts with a stationary environment
examples: DQN, PPO on MuJoCo

name: Cooperative multi-agent
positive_test: several agents share one team reward
examples: VDN, QMIX, MAPPO, COMA

name: Competitive multi-agent
positive_test: agents' rewards are opposed, approximately zero-sum
examples: self-play in Go, CFR for poker, NFSP, AlphaStar league

name: Mixed-motive multi-agent
positive_test: rewards are neither identical nor strictly opposed
negative_test: a purely cooperative or purely zero-sum setting
examples: sequential social dilemmas, mixed-motive MARL, negotiation agents

name: Information available at execution
scope: to multi-agent or partially observed control
characteristic: what each agent can observe when acting, as opposed to when training
positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: information available at execution
examples: centralized, CTDE, decentralized

name: Centralized execution
positive_test: the acting policy conditions on global state at deployment
examples: joint-action controllers, centralized planners

name: Centralized training, decentralized execution
positive_test: global information is used only during training
negative_test: global information is used while acting
examples: MADDPG, MAPPO, QMIX, COMA

name: Fully decentralized
positive_test: no global information is used at any stage
examples: IQL, IPPO, independent learners

name: Required output or action space
scope: to any method whose output type is constrained
characteristic: what structure the method's output must have
positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: required output or action space
negative_test: a method indifferent to output type
examples: discrete, continuous, hybrid, structured

name: Discrete
positive_test: requires a finite enumerable set of outputs or actions
examples: DQN, Q-learning, top-k sampling, classification losses

name: Continuous
positive_test: requires a real-valued, differentiable output or action space
examples: DDPG, TD3, SAC continuous, CEM-MPC, regression losses

name: Hybrid or parameterised
positive_test: requires a mixture of discrete choice and continuous parameters
negative_test: a purely discrete or purely continuous space
examples: parameterised-action RL, hybrid action DDPG

name: Structured or sequential
positive_test: the output is a sequence, tree or graph scored jointly
negative_test: the output is a single label or scalar
examples: beam search, CRF Viterbi, structured SVM, constrained decoding

name: Determinism of the procedure's output
characteristic: whether repeated application with fixed inputs gives the same result
positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: determinism of the procedure's output
examples: deterministic, stochastic

name: Deterministic
positive_test: same inputs and same parameters always produce the same output
examples: greedy decoding, beam search, k-means given an initialisation, PCA

name: Stochastic
positive_test: the procedure samples internally, so outputs vary across seeds
negative_test: the only randomness is in data ordering
examples: top-p sampling, dropout, MCMC, Thompson sampling, diffusion sampling

name: Treatment of estimate uncertainty
characteristic: what the procedure returns about its own uncertainty
positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: treatment of estimate uncertainty
negative_test: a procedure that returns no estimate
examples: point, interval, posterior, ensemble

name: Point estimate
positive_test: returns a single parameter or prediction with no dispersion
examples: SGD-trained networks, OLS point estimates, k-means centroids

name: Frequentist interval or test
positive_test: returns an interval or decision with a stated long-run error rate
examples: bootstrap CIs, conformal intervals, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests

name: Posterior distribution
positive_test: returns or samples an explicit posterior over parameters or functions
negative_test: returns an empirical spread across runs
examples: GP posteriors, MCMC samples, variational posteriors, SWAG, Bayesian NN

name: Empirical ensemble spread
positive_test: expresses uncertainty as disagreement among independently obtained predictors
negative_test: expresses it through an explicit posterior
examples: deep ensembles, bagging variance, MC dropout as approximation, snapshot ensembles

name: Formal guarantee claimed
scope: when the method is accompanied by a theorem
characteristic: what kind of mathematical statement the method comes with
positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: formal guarantee claimed
examples: convergence, regret, consistency, coverage, certification, approximation, unbiasedness

name: Convergence guarantee
positive_test: proves convergence to a stationary or optimal point under stated conditions
examples: FISTA rates, SVRG rates, convex SGD rates, ADMM convergence

name: Regret bound
positive_test: bounds cumulative loss relative to the best fixed or dynamic comparator
examples: UCB1, EXP3, LinUCB, online mirror descent, Thompson-sampling regret

name: Statistical consistency or asymptotic normality
positive_test: proves the estimate converges to the truth as sample size grows
examples: MLE consistency, doubly robust estimators, TMLE, double ML, M-estimation theory
notes: the main guarantee in the causal branch

name: Finite-sample coverage
positive_test: guarantees a stated coverage probability at finite sample size
examples: split conformal prediction, conformal risk control, distribution-free intervals

name: Certified robustness
positive_test: proves invariance of the prediction within a stated input region
examples: randomised smoothing, IBP, CROWN, convex relaxations

name: Approximation ratio
positive_test: proves a bounded ratio to the optimum of a hard combinatorial objective
negative_test: proves no bound on solution quality
examples: greedy submodular 1-1/e, k-means++ expected ratio, k-center greedy

name: Unbiasedness
positive_test: the estimator's expectation equals the target quantity
negative_test: the estimator is biased but lower variance
examples: REINFORCE score-function estimator, IPS, Horvitz-Thompson, unbiased MLMC
notes: often the explicit selling point over a biased rival

name: Separable-model production
characteristic: what artifact, if any, survives the run
positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: separable-model production
examples: parametric, instance-based, transductive

name: Produces parameters
positive_test: emits a fixed-size parameter set runnable on new inputs without the training data
negative_test: needs the training data at prediction time
examples: SGD-trained networks, OLS coefficients, GMM parameters, random forests
notes: the models dimension has an entry

name: Keeps the data as the model
positive_test: prediction requires the stored training examples themselves
examples: k-NN, kernel SVM support vectors, KDE, LOESS, Gaussian processes
notes: the legal "algorithm with no model" case

name: Transductive, produces no reusable object
positive_test: produces an output only for the points it was given; new points need a refit
negative_test: produces a map applicable to unseen points
examples: t-SNE, spectral clustering, DBSCAN, label propagation, MDS, UMAP-without-transform

name: Function preservation
scope: to every procedure that reorganises or distributes an existing computation
characteristic: whether the procedure changes the function computed
positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: function preservation
notes: the withdrawn `numerics test` in its proper place: real information, but an attribute, never a scope rule

name: Exact
positive_test: produces the same result as the unreorganised computation, up to floating-point reassociation
examples: FlashAttention, gradient checkpointing, ZeRO

name: Approximating
positive_test: changes the result by a bounded or controlled amount
examples: mixed precision, post-training quantization, gradient compression

name: Alters the optimisation
positive_test: changes the trajectory the run follows, so the learned object differs
examples: FedAvg, local SGD, asynchronous updates
